concept.title: Create a Strong Password
concept.shortdesc: Common password attacks and best practices for creating strong, secure passwords that resist compromise.

conbody.p: Cybercriminals commonly steal passwords through phishing websites or obtain encrypted password databases from data breaches. If you reuse the same password across multiple accounts, a breach on a single external website puts your university and personal accounts at risk. Per the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), length is the most critical factor in password strength: NIST recommends passwords of at least 15 characters and prioritizes length over mandatory special characters or numbers. Combining multiple unrelated words into a memorable passphrase—such as a 15- to 18-character phrase—dramatically increases cracking resistance, and pairing your accounts with MFA or phishing-resistant passkeys provides the strongest defense.
